Because we had the false witnesses, false alibis, five false witnesses. In 1991, a group of people arrives for the first time in Vukovar, and some of them told you that it was the last time. Witnesses spoke to you honestly that they wouldn't even remember that occasion if it hadn't been for my investigator showing them the tape and, of course, why should they remember if they saw such an unimportant person in their lives as Slavko Dokmanovic? Take a group of witnesses for the very unimportant part; that's Backa Palanka in the morning. They recognise him on the tape. And at noon, they left. The other witnesses begin from that point, two from Vukovar, and other people who are not from Vukovar. The Prosecution accepts now that they reached VELEPROMET, that they took part in the meeting, they went on into town, and we should stop here. In 1991, Zoran Jevtovic was supposed to film and record and glorify the president of his municipality from Kladovo, and quite accidentally, he also records the image of Slavko Dokmanovic. If you accept that none of us were clairvoyant in 1991, because had we been clairvoyant, Dokmanovic and all of us, we would have made a 14-hour film, from the very moment he woke up that morning throughout the day, so that this would suit the purposes of everyone, including the Prosecutor. He was simply recording Lazarevic, and he accidentally filmed Dokmanovic. He didn't even know that he had filmed him. In response to the question of the Prosecutor, he said that he didn't even know that he was in that town. What of the man who went there to give humanitarian aid; what did he go there for? He is a liar, according to the Prosecutor, a man who is a doctor of sciences, the director of a radio station, a prominent citizen. He's a liar. It is so easy to transfer blame that way. The other one is Jovan Cvetkovic, this other liar, the president of the municipality of Jagodina. At that time, you have him on that film that was made by the BBC who had the courage to say to Milosevic then what he thought about this war in Vukovar and this entire affair. He had that kind of courage. He was president of the municipality of Jagodina. He is a lawyer. He is now retired. He's a liar now. Dragisic, a man who educates children, the director of a school, the principal of a school, from the other car, he is also a liar. And, naturally, Dokmanovic is a liar too. This has been said just like that. You know, it's like Ping-Pong. 126 an hour. Everybody's a liar. And now, when we are supposed to ascertain what Cakalic and Berghofer are saying, well, they are victims. So when the victim is not speaking the truth, then it is a victim. And when a witness, who sees a town for the first time in his life and for the first time in his life sees a face and he is reminded by a film that he has seen this and that, then he is called a liar. Why are they liars? Because they did not remember that they went back 375 metres. That's why they are liars. I repeat, when I got that tape from Lazarevic, I got it so that we could show, the tape could show where Dokmanovic was not. Not where he was. And, undeniably, at 15.42, Dokmanovic was not at Ovcara, and that is what I wanted to prove to this Honourable Court. I was not interested at all where this particular frame was at 15.42 and any other hour. But let us see what is the importance of this particular frame, this particular clip. Then comes Sljivancanin, and already in the morning he said, when the Rule 61 hearing was conducted, he said in the morning that he would kill everyone. But now, no. Now they say that he came to seek approval of the civilian authorities. And why is it said so? Because Dokmanovic is sitting here. If Sljivancanin was sitting here, then it would have been different. Now you want to have Dokmanovic responsible. For example, if he comes there to ask the Minister of Agriculture, Dokmanovic, to kill all these people in Ovcara, and now what happens? Dokmanovic, having passed this decision to kill all these people in Ovcara, 200 people. Why? Because he's a Serb. He's bloodthirsty; he's thirsty for the blood of Croats. He wants to kill the Croats, the Ustashas, as much as he can, as many as he can. A terrible person. A man with the past of a monster, as he was called. He is going to tour the city first and then, when he tours the city, then he leaves the city in the direction of Ovcara, and when he gets to a point, I don't know where, then again he goes back to Vukovar. From 15.36, knowing that he is supposed to go to kill 200 Ustashas, like any monster, he goes back to Vukovar. Had I known about this at 15.42, that he was going back, I would have gained an additional five minutes in the alibi because he needed time to get back and go back. So that suits the Defence better than had he proceeded further on. One more thing, Your Honours. Look at the distances involved. At 15.42, that is practically the same distance, 1.000 metres, just as if he were at Negoslavci, because the turning-off point for Negoslavci is there. So it's all the same, from here to there, from there to here. But a different question is: Why would he go there? And I never heard this from this entire story. We heard so many stories of the Prosecutor. It is certain that it was a conspiracy there. We don't have proof in writing. You have no proof at all. You have assumption. You just have talk and nothing else. This person, he is just the form of a man. Within a year, he has been killed. Look at him today. Look at what he looks like. Look at the McFadden report. You have killed this man over this one-year period of time. You have killed the man in him. And now, how do you want to go through these acrobatics? You know, I remember this illusion of going through the Great Wall of China, or whatever. Somehow, you know, you have to have some kind of logic, a life logic, but I haven't heard anything about this. Five liars were driving around, and he didn't see the car behind him. Had they waited for this other car, then this car would have joined up with them. That is probably the way it happened. A person, a bloodthirsty man who is going to kill 200 Ustashas, 200 Croats, he's walking around town. He goes out, he goes back; he goes out, he goes back. It is senseless. Where did you see this ever in your lifetime? For 35 years, I have been on this job and for 35 years, I have been seeking a logic in acts. Eight minutes are needed for Witness Dzuro to get from that place to Ovcara, but when he is driving 50 kilometres an hour and when he is driving along a road where there are no other vehicles and where he knows where he's going. From the recording itself, you can see that buses are coming. If Dokmanovic were, at that very same point in time, to jump into the car and to go there, he would have to join the column of buses, and buses do not go 50 kilometres an hour. So he needs more than eight minutes to get there. And then what does he do? He abruptly closes the door of his car, he runs fast, he hits two men, and he goes back. In order to spend two minutes there, and then he goes back, and then at Orolik, Susa and others see him, as they said. Abracadabra system. This is Mickey Mouse proof. One cannot speak that way. And now, what is the time that is relevant to the Prosecutor in terms of his witnesses? What does Berghofer say? At 2.15, 2.30, and the Dutch police has also corroborated Dokmanovic was there until 15.42, so this is to say that the tapes are accurate. 15.42. 16.15, it is already dark. And an additional eight minutes to drive up there, so 15.50, 25 minutes. Abracadabra. It would be magic to do all of that. But what do they say? The uniform of a lieutenant-colonel of the JNA, blue. Everybody is olive grey-green. No. Only Dokmanovic is wearing blue. Only the two of them. None of the honourable witnesses of the Prosecution did not see a single person wearing a blue uniform. Our expert showed what the uniform of an Air Force officer of the JNA looks like. Not like that at all. One of them, Berghofer, saw a zipper; the other one saw a cape. You can make many mistakes. But in the first statement that was made for the press which you have in the supporting material of the Prosecutor, he speaks about a navy blue uniform himself, and that is why the Prosecutor claimed that this was an airman's uniform. And then Williamson told Dokmanovic that he was there in Stajicevo as an officer, a reserve officer, I repeat, of the JNA, and when Witness S said that he was not an officer, then Williamson brought it down. He said, "Well, you were there as a soldier, not more than that." And Dokmanovic in front of you was asked whether in Stajicevo you were there as a reserve officer of the JNA. A reservist, an officer, not a soldier. I'll try to slow down. My paper blew away. Finally, the question that is raised here, the people I brought here were people who talked about stopping, they were stopped twice in a settlement. They don't know where this Negoslavci is. Remember, it is the first time in their lives they were there. How come that they are liars now? Because they did not remember a detail that perhaps they went back 370 metres? Only the first vehicle, not the second one. Because if the first car went back to wait for the other one, the other one never went back. I don't know how the Prosecutor draws the conclusion that both cars went back, and also those from the second car also said that they were with Dokmanovic all the time. In Orolik, they see him. In Negoslavci, they stop for a longer period of time. In Orolik, even longer. When you listen further on, the behaviour of Dokmanovic; is a normal man who is going to go and kill 200 persons before that? You have life experience. You have experience in courts of law. I mean, he is a man without a criminal record. He was a father even then. Now he is even a grandfather; then he wasn't a grandfather. And you saw in their petition what his fellow citizens wrote about him. Can that kind of person take part in the killing of 200 persons and then continue a conversation? Yes, he can, because he's a Serb. That is how I understood this because I heard that it was Serbs who were killing at Ovcara, and I say that it is criminals who were killing at Ovcara, not Serbs. I shall speak about punishment and sentencing, and Mr. Niemann referred to this, and I think it's a terrible thing to talk about this. You have a person with an impeccable past. Even Cakalic and Berghofer, look at what they say about his personality. Why didn't any one of them say that he played a key role? Look at the difference that the Prosecutors' investigators get when they talk to the witnesses and what the witnesses themselves say they said. When the Prosecutors' investigators speak to the witnesses, the witnesses talk about the key role of Dokmanovic, but in front of you, they say that accidentally he came up, out of curiosity. When the investigator of the Prosecution speaks to Witness S, and he says that he signed a statement saying that he was there as an officer in Stajicevo, Dokmanovic, and when he came to see you, he said he was some kind of soldier in some kind of uniform, and ultimately it was proven that this wasn't any uniform at all. Not a military uniform at any rate, this tape. And when I showed on the tape what kind of clothes Dokmanovic was wearing and they ask Wagenaar to come in. Why Wagenaar? To prove that the witnesses were not telling the truth, the witnesses for the Prosecution, so they are saying that their own witnesses are not telling the truth. But if these witnesses are saying what the time was -- time is a very important thing in this trial. Tadeusz Mazowieszki established that everything at Ovcara occurred within four hours' time, between 2.00 and 6.00 p.m., and the witness for the Prosecution shortened this period of time, between 2.15, 2.30 at the latest, up to 4.00 p.m., but they were already outside by 4.00 p.m. And what do they say further on? Slavko Dokmanovic is present when the buses are being emptied, and they are in the second bus, not the last one. But this is 14.30, up to 15.00 hours, and this is when Slavko Dokmanovic is in town. He is giving an interview to Tomasevic. When they get out, it is still daylight. Cakalic and Berghofer, I mean. When you look at the sun at 15.36 on this famous tape, you can see that the sun is setting. The Prosecutor has heard all of that from the ABi, they heard it from the police in The Hague here, but they were looking for someone to say something different, but they didn't find anyone to say that. At 16.15, at 4.15 p.m., it is dark. Cakalic and Berghofer said that before dark, all of this was happening. So now, try to put Slavko Dokmanovic's behaviour into this context, from 15.42 until sundown, so that this could all fit into the statements made by honourable men, Cakalic and Berghofer, and I say even now that they probably had the wrong impression because there was an officer there with a moustache and also an officer wearing an olive green-grey uniform, the one who is blowing the whistle and whatever, that is mentioned in different statements, and when it suits the Prosecutor's purposes, then it is Mrkic, but, no, that is not important. It is possible that these persons were replaced. How come they only remember that it was him and that they were wrong in terms of the time, in terms of the uniform? They even didn't see him at the same place. Finally, this last evidence that I accepted from the Prosecution today, here today, in order to help expedite this trial, and even more than that, I want to have the truth, that Witness Q says that he brought these two persons in front of the hangar because whoever got into the hangar didn't leave it after that. That is to say, that Witnesses Berghofer and Cakalic were not even in the hangar, according to Witness Q; and that is to say that Dokmanovic could not have been both inside and outside. Once in the statement and here differently. The witnesses that the Prosecutor calls liars only forgot that perhaps they stopped and went back 375 metres, everything else fitted in; and also the distance Witness Dzuro said matches that on the film, that is their walk through Vukovar. And that is how we have reached this point of a hocus-pocus. How well Dokmanovic does this magic, when you hear his voice, 15.42, run into these two minutes and commit these six serious violations of humanitarian law and go back then and continue living peacefully and continue travelling along. That is your task, Your Honours. If that is why this court was established, I really have nothing further to add. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Fila. I assume both parties have completed their presentation of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Therefore, pursuant to Rule 87, we will now declare the hearing closed, and we will deliberate in private. I am happy, Mr. Fila, that you did appreciate that we were very keen to have an expeditious trial, and we will try to be consistent. No, no, it's all right. Even this afternoon, we were rather speedy. Since you like Roman law and Latin as much as I do, let me quote a Roman saying. A Roman, as you know, said: Bis dat qui cito dat. "He gives twice who gives quickly." So therefore we promise that we will try to deliberate as soon as possible and come to a conclusion as soon as possible, and we expect that it is most likely that we will probably render our judgement in two weeks' time. We will let you know in due time. There being no other matters, we will now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: sine die at 3.52 p.m.
